clue.text: Railway staff in station, closer?

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so the staff go within the station word

parts.note: a stop is a station on a railway line
the people who work a train are its crew

explanation.surface: A railway worker standing in a station is asked whether they will be closing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by function: a bottle's screw cap is literally something that closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw cap seals a jar or bottle, so it is playfully described as something that shuts things.

clue.text: Bet it's a flat-bottomed boat!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wager, especially a small speculative one
second meaning: a square-ended river craft pushed along with a pole

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a punt is both a gamble and the pole-propelled boat used on the rivers at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal British slang for a wager and also names the shallow pole-driven river craft.

clue.text: Delicate area, place of worship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the soft, vulnerable side of the head beside the eye
second meaning: a building dedicated to a god

explanation.walkthrough: The side of the skull there is thin, which is why it counts as a delicate spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically it is the flat sensitive region at each side of the forehead; religiously it is a sacred building.

clue.text: Fish: fifty caught by father

indicators.note: something caught is held inside its captor, so the number sits within the parent word

parts.note: the father of an institution or movement is its founder
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A father lands a fish, fifty of them perhaps, on a day out angling.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a flatfish, a common edible species found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Sweet gag?

parts.note: surface reading: a pleasant joke
setter's reading: a hard candy so big that it plugs the mouth, a gag that is also a confection

explanation.walkthrough: Gag looks like a joke but means something that stops speech; gob is British slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hard round sugary ball that fills the mouth, so the confection literally silences whoever is sucking it.

clue.text: Indicate economy originally in good health going the other way

indicators.note: travelling the opposite direction, so the whole string is read from the end back to the start
originally points to the start, so only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: the first letter of economy
someone toned is fit and in good condition

explanation.surface: A report says the economy, at first in good health, then went into reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to signify or point it out, a straightforward synonym for showing or meaning.

clue.text: Maestro adding last of paint to drunken cherubs

indicators.note: a drunken group staggers about out of order, so these letters get rearranged
last of means only the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of paint
taken as written

explanation.surface: A master painter adds a final dab to a canvas of tipsy cherubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Maestro suggests an old master painter, given the paint, but here it is a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Schubert, the Austrian composer of lieder and symphonies, is a great musician and so a maestro.

clue.text: From the audience, seat chucked out

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a throne is a royal seat

explanation.surface: A spectator's seat in the audience gets thrown out of the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chucked out has been tossed or hurled, past participle of the verb meaning to fling.

clue.text: Eye someone gorgeous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who looks, an observer or watcher
second meaning: informal word for a very attractive person

explanation.walkthrough: Eye reads as a verb, to ogle a beauty, but it is a noun for the person doing the watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who watches, and colloquially a strikingly good-looking person, especially a beautiful woman.

clue.text: Direction taken into Lowestoft

indicators.note: the letters are swallowed up inside the town name, sitting within it

parts.note: letters three to six of the town name

explanation.surface: Someone is given directions into Lowestoft, a fishing town on the Suffolk coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowestoft is the most easterly town in Britain, which makes the other compass point a sly choice.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal compass points, the way the sun sets.

clue.text: Super coins forged, items struck

indicators.note: forged metal is beaten into new shape, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Splendid counterfeit coins are forged, then struck at the mint.
explanation.walkthrough: Struck suggests minting coins; here it means instruments that are hit, like drums and cymbals.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestral section of drums, cymbals and similar instruments played by hitting them is collectively named that.

clue.text: Basic article in magazine, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: main, fundamental, as in a dietary mainstay
second meaning: the small wire fastener binding the pages of a periodical

explanation.walkthrough: Article in magazine looks like a feature story; it is a physical item found in the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means chief or principal; as a noun it is a bent wire clip holding sheets together.

clue.text: Novel aprons I use for cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone explains the aprons they put on to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasion is Jane Austen's final completed book, published in 1817, so it is a work of fiction.

clue.text: Vulnerable writer after extra opportunities, initially

indicators.note: after sends the writer to follow the other pieces, so it comes last rather than first

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, scoring an extra run

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the opening letter of the preceding word counts

parts.note: the first letter of opportunities
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A writer is seeking more chances to get started.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat, and a wide is one kind; after places the writer at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left wide open is exposed to attack or criticism, an idiom for being defenceless.

clue.text: Stealing some company car, I promptly retired

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
some means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: a run of letters spanning the end of company to the start of promptly

explanation.surface: An employee pinches a firm's car, then quickly retires from the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or the illegal copying of creative work; either way it means theft.

clue.text: Decorative work bagging point, finally — mark on score

indicators.note: bagging something means capturing it and holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: crochet is lacework made with a hooked needle

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: the final letter of point

explanation.surface: A needlework piece wins a point at a craft show and is marked on the judges' score.
explanation.walkthrough: Score means a written piece of music here, not a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is the quarter note in musical notation, a symbol written on sheet music.

clue.text: Hollow weapon, it getting loaded with first of pellets

indicators.note: a weapon loaded with ammunition holds it inside, so one piece goes into the others

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
taken as written

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of pellets

explanation.surface: An air gun is being loaded with pellets.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollow reads as an adjective describing the gun; it is a noun for a cavity of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder where the arm joins the body, so it is an anatomical cavity.

clue.text: Short jacket on Welsh girl from North Africa

indicators.note: something short lacks its end, so the final letter of the garment is cut off

parts.note: a tunic is a close-fitting jacket, especially in a uniform
Siân is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl wears a short jacket brought back from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country on the North African coast, and the adjective describes something from there.

clue.text: Backbone in apparition?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: courage, determination, strength of character
second meaning: a ghost or phantom

explanation.walkthrough: Backbone suggests the spine, but here it is grit, as in showing some mettle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both courage or mettle and a disembodied ghost that might haunt a house.

clue.text: Physician, American senior in TV programme

parts.note: doc is short for doctor
US is short for the United States
OAP is the British abbreviation for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An American doctor and an elderly patient appear on a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A docusoap is a fly-on-the-wall documentary series following real people, a kind of television show.

clue.text: Threatening words when loser upset over conclusion of referee

indicators.note: something upset is knocked into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of referee

explanation.surface: A sore loser angrily threatens the referee after the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over means placed above, so the shuffled letters sit on top of the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is tacked onto a demand as a warning of consequences, as in pay up, or else.

clue.text: Leave single thread

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to abandon someone, leaving them stuck
second meaning: one fibre or filament

explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means to maroon, like a ship on a shore; as a noun, one length of fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone stuck without means of moving on, or one filament twisted with others into rope.

clue.text: Sweetheart wanting gold after diamonds, say

parts.note: diamonds is an example of a suit in a pack of cards
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A lover wants gold to go with the diamonds he has bought.
explanation.walkthrough: After puts the gold at the end; say marks diamonds as an example of a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, so he is her admirer or beau.

clue.text: Cowgirl: she trained dog

indicators.note: training reshapes and reorders, so these letters are drilled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cowgirl has trained her dog to herd cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, corgis were bred as cattle-herding dogs in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh corgi is a short-legged herding breed, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Chest in smithereens

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bosom, or a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: Chest reads as a box that might be smashed; it is the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a woman's chest measurement and is also informal for broken or wrecked.

clue.text: Lure, a bit fishy!

indicators.note: fishy means suspect or not right, so the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler admits the fly used to tempt the fish is slightly suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Fishy doubles as the anagram signal and a nod to angling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is food on a hook used to tempt fish, and more generally any enticement.

clue.text: Dust and rock on the beach?

parts.note: ash is the powdery residue left after burning
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Sand and pebbles are what you find on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land rather than at sea, so on the coast or sand by the water.

clue.text: Hot current circling capital of Rwanda

indicators.note: circling something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: current affairs are topical ones

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening letter, the only one used

parts.note: the first letter of Rwanda

explanation.surface: A hot ocean current flows around the capital of Rwanda.
explanation.walkthrough: Current looks like a flow of water or electricity, but it means up to date; capital is not Kigali but a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical climates near the equator are sweltering, so the adjective describes heat and humidity.
